items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: I played with Eddie Mallory. ... I joined Eddie Mallory's band

ctx.x: Yeah, because I was instrumental in getting Everett the gig with Eddie South, and you played -- where did you play? Club DeLisa, and ...
I played with Eddie Mallory. Yeah.

When I came to Chicago --and I have to lead into that, but coming out of Detroit, I met Roy Eldridge in Detroit, he was based there as a young fellow in those days, and oh, let's see, Milt Buckner was, I think he might have -- well, I don't even know if he was born yet, but his older brother, Ted, was around.

items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: in Chicago, it was still a spit away from the Milt Senior band to play with Eddie Mallory, an excellent lead trumpet player.

ctx.x:
Yes, but that was later -- after the Gold Coast job folded, then I joined Eddie Mallory's band and that's where I worked with Budd Johnson and Keg Johnson. But my brother and I split up ways then, because when I went with Milt Senior, he stayed on with the Speed Webb band, so by the time I got to Chicago, I was in Toledo, I was on my own, away from Gus. Since we left school together, we had been together until that period in Toledo.

But in Chicago, it was still a spit away from the Milt Senior band to play with…
And we had a good band, too.
